entry.title: Ironwood · Day 5: The Woman Who Wrote Her Round on an Envelope in the Rain
entry.content:
Sunday 8 July 2046, night

Council drains: do not enter standing water. Report any cover that has lifted.Civic Works notice, cable-tied to the towpath railing at Lockyer Street

Isabel came to Linden Rise Centre at five to ten that morning, after a tram, a train and a bus, with two fingers of her right hand swollen purple under the gauze. At the culvert under the ring road she and Amara Nwosu, who was fifteen, tested a corrected reading on the dial by the bench, then went into the drain lake together. The static led them to the grate, where a thread came out and slid toward the box in Amara's hands. Isabel pulled Amara back by her hood. The box sank under the grate and could not be recovered.

Amara then called her staff and walked the culvert bank, where six threads came out and were burned or pinned. Isabel had stood closer to the bars than Amara and was not targeted. The signal dropped to a low hum under the ring road. Isabel said the heart could be left for another day. Amara wrote a figure on the back of her hand and went back up the path with Isabel to catch the bus.

In Kell's Lane, Natalie chalked a line along the wall from the downpipe, marking the seam that had crept toward the fire stair. Her right hand would no longer close past halfway, and she could not find the root under the stair. She left the chalk on the bottom step, with a question mark at the end of the line. Mrs Vella told Isabel, when she came for the key at half past four, that Natalie had been there. Isabel found the chalk in the rain, tried to photograph it, and redrew the line from memory in her left hand. Mrs Vella said she would ring the council's emergency line that night and kept the key.

At seven, Natalie went out to the tram stop grate, which was flooding. On the towpath near the bridge she fell into the canal and lost her phone. She climbed out at the hatch, sat in the tram shelter, and wrote directions for her round on the back of her letter from her mother in Port Ellery.

Log

  • Rain comes in off the river in the afternoon and keeps on through the night, and Ruth rings Natalie in the evening.
  • The seam at the north cut knits most of the way over and what is left creeps along Kell's Lane toward the fire stair.
    • The north cut's seam closes over +1
  • Amara holds the mended box to the culvert grate and gets a steady reading just under the third mark, then Isabel pulls her back by the hood and the box goes into the drain lake and sinks under the grate. (success-with-cost, risky, rolled 1, 5 (two dice keeping the best))
    • Amara Nwosu lost the signal meter, sunk under the culvert grate in the drain lake with its reading
    • the signal meter: now gone
    • Isabel now believes: Amara's reading at the grate was real, just under the third mark.
  • Isabel wades after Amara into the drain lake, behind her, after Amara goes straight to the grate with the box despite having been told to take the nerves first and never walk up alone. (failure, risky, rolled 6, 1 (no dice, so two keeping the worst))
    • Isabel lost her place at the front of the walk, the one she came an hour and a half to hold
    • Isabel shaken
    • Amara Nwosu now believes: She kept all three of Isabel's rules, since she told Isabel before she moved.
  • Amara walks the culvert bank slowly and draws six nerved threads out of the pipe, pinning and leaning each one until the signal drops to a hum under the ring road. (clean, risky, rolled 6, 2 (two dice keeping the best))
    • Amara Nwosu buoyed
    • Isabel now believes: The nerved threads go after whoever is moving, not whoever stands nearest the culvert.
  • Isabel asks Amara whether her feet have stood at a blight before, and Amara answers with an unfinished story about reading and forums, and Isabel drops the question and turns to the road. (failure, risky, rolled 2, 2 (no dice, so two keeping the worst))
    • Isabel lost the answer she came for about whether Amara's feet had stood at a blight before, which Amara kept
  • Natalie chalks a metre of the crooked seam line along Kell's Lane by feel, then the staff slips in her scalded right palm and her grip stops closing past halfway, and she chalks three more metres by eye and leaves the stub on the fire stair step. (failure, risky, rolled 3, 2 (no dice, so two keeping the worst))
    • Natalie lost her grip on the staff: her right hand will not close past halfway, and the staff came out of it
    • the chalk stub: now at the north cut
  • Mrs Vella presses Natalie on who is coming for her drains and Natalie names Isabel, saying to tell her and not Natalie, and Mrs Vella gets the name but loses the say she wanted over her own drains. (success-with-cost, controlled, rolled 5 (one die))
    • Mrs Vella lost the say over her own drains, which Natalie handed on to Isabel
    • Mrs Vella now believes: Natalie is handing the drains to Isabel and is not coming herself.
  • Isabel tells Mrs Vella about the warm mark under the block and the thing that went round behind her by the bins, and Mrs Vella takes the key back, refuses to let it out of her house again, and shuts the door. (failure, risky, rolled 1, 2 (no dice, so two keeping the worst))
    • Isabel lost the cellar key, which Mrs Vella took back and will not let out of her house again
    • the key: now with Mrs Vella
    • Mrs Vella now believes: The thing from the cellar drain went round behind Isabel and off along the pipe, possibly toward her own house.
  • Isabel photographs the chalk line in the rain and gets only white smears, then picks up the chalk stub and redraws the line from memory without her staff, crooked, with no question mark. (failure, risky, rolled 6, 2 (no dice, so two keeping the worst))
    • Isabel lost the photographs of Natalie's chalk line, which came out as white smears, and her memory of where the question mark was
    • the chalk stub: now with Isabel
    • Isabel now believes: Natalie is putting the lane in order before she goes away, not taking it off her.
  • Natalie walks the towpath toward the tram-stop grate, slides off the bank into the rising canal to her hips, drops her phone in the water, and drags herself out onto the path. (failure, desperate, rolled 2, 1 (no dice, so two keeping the worst))
    • Natalie lost her phone, dropped into the canal, and with it her mother's number, which she never learned by heart
    • Natalie shaken
    • Natalie's phone: now gone
    • her mother's letter: now with Natalie

entry.title: Ironwood · Day 4: The Stall Woman Gave a Girl a Tomato and Asked Nothing
entry.content:
Saturday 7 July 2046, morning

Keep off the drains on Linnet Lane. Ask before you go down.Handwritten note pinned inside the lobby of Kell's Lane block, 4 Kell's Lane

On Saturday morning Amara Nwosu walked the Tangle's wall with her mother, who was checking the site for Second Growth before Tuesday's consultation. Her mother had brought her because of the injured wrist. Amara carried a meter in her satchel. A Second Growth van was parked on Lockyer Street, and the box pulled hard against her hip as she passed it.

At the gate stall, Hyejin Park asked why the hall was going up at the Tangle. Hyejin had sent Amara three messages after she posted online. Amara's mother said she would answer on Tuesday. Hyejin said three hundred names would come, and her mother wrote the number down. Amara turned her back to the stall and took a reading at the gate. The needle reached the second mark. She could not tell how much of that was the bent pin. Hyejin noticed the box and the dressing. Amara's mother said her daughter had built it. Hyejin gave Amara the reddest tomato and said it was on the house. Amara did not eat it.

At midday Isabel went into the block cellar on Kell's Lane with her staff. Her right hand had not closed past halfway since the day before, so her phone slid to the floor. She followed a crooked seam across the slab to an iron inspection cover and lifted it with her left hand. Below it was a warm stain on the brick joint, and nothing else. Then the static came from behind her, near the door, and moved away before she could reach it. The lid came down on two fingers of her right hand. Isabel told Mrs Vella the source had gone.

In the afternoon rain Natalie went to check the grate under the tram stop, which flooded first in any rain. She passed the Tangle's gate, where Hyejin asked her to come inside. Natalie refused. She pressed her scalded right palm against the iron bar until the wound opened, and said she knew where Hyejin had been. She paid for her beans by phone, though Hyejin wanted nothing, and worked the grate from the kerb with her staff.

After eight that night Isabel went to Natalie's flat on Weir Street. Natalie's right hand was in new gauze. Isabel told her about the cellar. Natalie said Isabel would work the Salter's Lane grate alone on Tuesday at five. Isabel asked what was in the inside pocket of Natalie's coat. Natalie said it was a letter from home. Isabel left into the rain.

Log

  • Saturday 7 July: Hyejin's stall is out at the Tangle, with the council's notice about the hall curling in its window.
  • Amara took a reading off the Tangle gate and wall with the box while Mum was at the stall, and the needle climbed to the second mark; Hyejin saw the box and the dressing on Amara's wrist and said nothing aloud. (success-with-cost, risky, rolled 4 (one die))
    • the signal meter: now with Amara Nwosu
    • Amara Nwosu now believes: Hyejin only saw a box and a girl with a sore wrist, and doesn't know what the box is for.
    • Hyejin Park now believes: Amara is reading the Tangle's gate and wall for blight with that box, and the scald on her wrist is a blight's bite.
  • Hyejin pressed Chioma to say why the hall had to go on the Tangle's edge; Chioma gave three versions of Tuesday, and Hyejin gave her the figure of three hundred names, which Chioma wrote down in her notebook. (failure, controlled, rolled 3 (one die))
    • The council votes on the hall +1
    • Amara Nwosu now believes: Mum has Hyejin's count of three hundred names to plan the room around.
  • Isabel followed the root's static across the cellar floor to an iron inspection cover, lifted it and found only a warm stain on the brick, then the root felt her come from behind, ran under the side wall, and the lid came down on the first two fingers of her right hand. (failure, risky, rolled 5, 2 (no dice, so two keeping the worst))
    • Isabel hurt: The lid came down on the first two fingers of her right hand against the iron rim, and the knuckles went hot and then wet under the gauze.
    • Isabel now believes: The root has grown nerves again and can feel her coming across a floor.
    • Mrs Vella now believes: The thing from the cellar drain has gone under the block, and the Linnet Lane side of it is unsafe for the little ones.
  • Hyejin pressed Natalie to come through the gate into the Tangle and look; Natalie refused, said she knew where Hyejin had been, took her hand off the bar, and paid for the beans at the stall's reader by phone though Hyejin said she owed nothing, and Hyejin turned her back. (failure, risky, rolled 1 (one die))
    • Hyejin Park estranged from Natalie
    • Hyejin Park now believes: Natalie can't take her eyes off the bridge; the pull still has her.
  • Natalie kept her face on Hyejin while the pull toward the bridge rose in her, holding the wet gate, and the soft middle of the scald across her palm opened against the iron. (success-with-cost, risky, rolled 6, 4 (no dice, so two keeping the worst))
    • Natalie hurt: The soft middle of the scald across her right palm reopened against the wet iron of the gate.
  • Isabel asked what was in Natalie's coat and what Tuesday really was; Natalie said only that it was a letter from home and that Tuesday was Salter's Lane if it thawed, and Isabel said Natalie was keeping her out of the book and asked whether she could be trusted. (failure, risky, rolled 6, 1 (no dice, so two keeping the worst))
    • Isabel ashamed
    • her mother's letter: now with Natalie
    • Isabel now believes: Natalie's letter is from home in Port Ellery.
  • Natalie gave Isabel Salter's Lane alone for Tuesday at five, saying she would be at home in bed, and Isabel took it as being let go, said she would do it, and went out past the coat into the rain. (failure, risky, rolled 6, 3 (no dice, so two keeping the worst))
    • Natalie estranged from Isabel
    • Isabel now believes: Natalie will be at home in bed on Tuesday, not at Salter's Lane.

entry.title: Ironwood · Day 3: The Wall Closed Behind the Staff Before the Girl Was Called Off It
entry.content:
Friday 6 July 2046, morning

Tell me before you move. Don't leave it to the last minute.Scrawled on a fridge magnet note, Rowan Crescent

Natalie walked her Friday round from Weir Street at a quarter to five, through a hard frost. At Chandler's Row, Salter's Lane and the Bell Street drain she cleared small roots with her staff. The grate in Salter's Lane would not clear: the cold had driven the blight into the iron bars, and when she leaned on it the copper came back up her arms. Her right palm was scalded where she had pressed on the grate for about twelve minutes. She left the root there to wait for a thaw.

At the Tangle's wall she read the council notice in the stall window: a public consultation on a substrate hall, Tuesday 10 July, at the Canal Community Rooms. At the bridge she went down the bank toward the patch by the canal, slipped on the ice, and put her left boot into the water up to the shin. She came back up the bank on her hands and reopened the scald. She did the rest of the round with a wet, freezing trouser leg, and did not go home to change.

At Kell's Lane, Isabel opened the wall from the downpipe with her staff, held in her left hand, her right hand scalded and gauzed. Natalie waited under the fire stair. Before Isabel reached the stair, Natalie went in, and the end of the root she had pinned there went grey. The seam closed back along the wall behind Isabel, and the root ran into the drain at the foot of the downpipe and went under the building. Isabel had not called Natalie to the wall. She told Mrs Vella to keep the children off the downpipe and the drain.

At Rowan Crescent, Amara Nwosu repaired her meter on the kitchen table. She fixed a cold joint and reseated the needle, which now rests slightly high because the pin is bent. Her mother found the scald on her wrist and dressed it, then told her to attend the consultation evening on Tuesday. Amara agreed. She texted Isabel that she had mended the box and asked her to come on Sunday to watch her hold it to the grate.

Afterwards Natalie and Isabel went back to Isabel's flat. Natalie rinsed Isabel's hand under the cold tap and asked how she would come at the Salter's Lane grate once the thaw arrived, and then the rest of the round. Isabel answered. When Natalie said someone ought to be there for Amara on Sunday, Isabel told her she hadn't been asking. Natalie wound clean gauze round the hand, and left, having made one mug of tea. Isabel texted Amara that she should not go near the grate until Isabel was there.

Log

  • The first hard frost of the winter came down before dawn on Friday 6 July and turned the old core white.
  • Natalie leaned her staff on the Salter's Lane grate for twelve minutes, but the frost held the blight locked in the iron, so the copper came back cold and left a scald across her right palm while the root stayed where it was. (failure, risky, rolled 1 (one die))
    • Natalie hurt: a copper-coloured scald across the base of her right palm, over the callus, wet and soft in the middle
    • Natalie now believes: The root in the Salter's Lane grate will sit in the iron until a thaw loosens it, and only then can it be cut.
  • Natalie walked the towpath toward the patch by the bridge, went down the frozen bank anyway, broke through the ice into the canal to her shin, and climbed back up on her hands, reopening the palm scald on the grass. (failure, risky, rolled 1 (one die))
    • Natalie hurt: the scald on her palm reopened on the frozen grass, and her left leg was soaked and froze from the knee down
  • Isabel argued at the north cut to take the stair end herself, and Natalie refused, keeping the pinned root for her own hand, so Isabel gave the stair end up and was left to watch. (failure, risky, rolled 2, 1 (no dice, so two keeping the worst))
    • Isabel lost the stair end at Kell's Lane, which Natalie kept for herself
  • Isabel held the crooked seam open along the wall four metres to the downpipe, but the root slipped past her staff into the drain under the block as the seam closed behind her, and her shape gave out so she was left kneeling on the cobbles. (failure, risky, rolled 1, 4 (no dice, so two keeping the worst))
    • The north cut's seam closes over +1
    • Isabel lost her shape, which slipped off her when she was spent and left her with nothing in her hands
    • Isabel now believes: The root has gone into the drain under the building, out of reach from the lane.
    • Mrs Vella now believes: The drain at the foot of the downpipe is unsafe for the little ones.
  • Amara reseated the needle on its pin and rewelded the cold joint, so the box held together, but the needle now rests a hair above zero before her mother's feet reached the stairs. (success-with-cost, controlled, rolled 4 (one die))
    • Amara Nwosu lost a true zero on the signal box; the needle now rests a hair high on its straightened pin, so its readings will run that much high
  • Mum found the scald on Amara's wrist and held her hand under the lamp, and Amara's story about the iron and her answer that she was on her own didn't hold, so Tuesday became the canal rooms with her mother. (failure, risky, rolled 3 (one die))
    • Amara Nwosu lost Tuesday to herself until eleven at the culvert, which is now a seat at the back of the canal rooms with her mother
    • Chioma Nwosu now believes: Amara was alone in the water at the culvert.
    • Chioma Nwosu now believes: The burn on Amara's wrist is from the soldering iron on Wednesday night.
  • Natalie walked Isabel through the old-core round in order and asked why Tuesday; Isabel gave the whole round and said the thaw was due Tuesday, and Natalie took the answer without pressing. (clean, risky, rolled 6 (one die))
    • Natalie buoyed
    • Isabel now believes: Natalie is keeping something back about Tuesday.
  • Isabel asked Natalie to name what she had done well at the cut and to stay on for the morning; Natalie answered only the hand, saying Isabel stopped when it went, and left on her wet boot to walk the old core alone. (failure, risky, rolled 3, 3 (no dice, so two keeping the worst))
    • Isabel lost Natalie's company for the rest of the morning, as Natalie went off alone to walk the old core

entry.title: Ironwood · Day 2: The Culvert Grate Where Amara Walked Out Ahead of the Staff
entry.content:
Thursday 5 July 2046, morning

Lost a cat near the Linden Rise culvert, grey with one white ear. Please ring before it gets dark.Handwritten notice taped to a bus shelter, Linden Rise

Isabel travelled out to Linden Rise by train and bus, arriving just after ten. She met Amara Nwosu at the drain lake by the culvert, where Amara had repaired a faulty meter the night before. Isabel waded in to deal with a blight lodged behind the grate, and told Amara to stay at the edge.

Amara moved along the bank instead, drawing the threads out of the pipe after her, and Isabel took them one at a time as they cleared the bars. One thread lashed across the back of Isabel's hand as she gripped the bars, leaving a scald across her knuckles. Amara was also scalded, a thin mark running up her forearm from the wrist. The heart of the blight sits under the ring road and Isabel did not reach it. She said it could not feel them without its nerves and would keep. Amara admitted she had read about this on forums, and Isabel said she had been standing like someone who had done it before.

Isabel then travelled into the north lanes and went to Kell's Lane. A seam she had opened on Tuesday night had closed crooked, running under a fire stair and along the wall to a downpipe, about four metres. Working on it cut a second scald across her hand. She left it unfinished and said she would return the next morning.

Natalie walked the canal path in the evening and met Isabel outside the community rooms by the canal at about eight. Isabel described the culvert and Kell's Lane. Natalie agreed to meet her at Kell's Lane at seven the next morning, after her round, and to take the stair end while Isabel worked the rest. Natalie also said she had told Elspeth Hale that Isabel would bring the jar of ash to Garnet Street, and that Elspeth would hold it for her.

Log

  • Thursday grey weather hangs over the drain lake at Linden Rise, still over its path at the culvert, while Friends of the Tangle meet at the canal rooms and the Back Room plays at the Exchange.
  • Isabel tells Natalie she will finish the north cut alone tomorrow and take the pesto jar of ash to Garnet Street herself, and Natalie agrees that both are Isabel's. (clean, risky, rolled 6 (one die))
    • Isabel buoyed
    • the pesto jar: now with Isabel
    • Isabel now believes: Natalie has handed her the north cut and the jar and means it.
  • Amara steps down into the drain water with her signal box ahead of the rules, and Isabel, who could have caught her sleeve, lets her go, so the threads in the pipe turn toward the girl and the needle climbs to the stop. (failure, risky, rolled 2 (one die))
    • Amara Nwosu lost the rules she'd been given: she went out ahead of them, and the blight came round to her
    • Isabel lost her hold on Amara: the girl went out past the edge Isabel had told her to keep, and Isabel let her
    • Amara Nwosu shaken
    • Isabel now believes: Amara will walk on ahead of any rule she is given.
  • Amara holds the signal box to the grate for a true reading, and the needle lifts to the stop and then drops loose at the bottom, off its pin, so the meter gives no proof. (failure, risky, rolled 2 (one die))
    • Amara Nwosu lost her signal meter's reading: the needle came off its pin, so the box gives no proof
    • the signal meter: now with Amara Nwosu
  • Isabel pins the nerved threads one by one as Amara walks them out along the bank, and the last thread whips back over Amara's wrist and across the back of Isabel's hand, leaving Isabel a scald. (success-with-cost, risky, rolled 4, 5 (two dice keeping the best))
    • Isabel hurt: a scald across her raw knuckles, copper-coloured and weeping
    • Amara Nwosu now believes: Walking slowly along the bank draws the nerved threads out of the pipe to the one with the staff.
    • Isabel now believes: The nerves follow whoever moves closest, which can be a girl walking the bank rather than the one holding the staff.
  • Amara keeps her two earlier cuts hidden, but her feet move as if they have stood at a blight before, and Isabel sees it and asks nothing she can answer. (failure, risky, rolled 1 (one die))
    • Amara Nwosu lost her secret of the two cuts, which Isabel now half knows
    • Amara Nwosu now believes: Isabel now knows that her feet have stood at a blight before.
    • Isabel now believes: Amara has stood at a nerved blight before.
  • Natalie asks Elspeth to wait for Isabel to bring the ash herself, and Elspeth agrees to hold the Hundred and Fourth without taking the jar from Natalie's hand, telling her to say the step is here. (clean, risky, rolled 6 (one die))
    • Natalie buoyed
    • Elspeth Hale now believes: Isabel is the one teaching the Linden Rise girl.
    • Elspeth Hale now believes: Isabel will bring the ash to her herself.
  • Isabel finds the crooked seam under the fire stair, follows its true line four metres along the wall to the downpipe, and takes a scald from the second knuckle to the wrist bone as it pushes back up her staff. (success-with-cost, risky, rolled 4 (one die))
    • Isabel hurt: a scald from the second knuckle to the wrist bone, crossing the first, as wide as a pencil
    • Isabel now believes: The true line runs under the fire stair and along the wall about four metres to the downpipe, and will take an hour to hold open.
    • Mrs Vella now believes: The girl from the second floor is hurt and won't say how.
  • Natalie says she will take the stair end at Kell's Lane tomorrow and do the hard part under the stair herself, and Isabel is left to watch, having given up finishing the cut alone. (failure, risky, rolled 1 (one die))
    • Isabel lost her plan to finish the north cut alone, given up for the stair end and the root under it
    • Isabel now believes: Natalie will take the stair end and leave the rest of the cut for Isabel to watch.
    • Natalie now believes: Isabel can't take the bit under the stair alone with her hand as it is.

entry.title: Ironwood · Day 1: The Answer Given in Daylight on the Canal Bank
entry.content:
Wednesday 4 July 2046, morning

DO NOT USE THE TOWPATH AFTER HEAVY RAIN.Council notice, cable-tied to the railing of the old canal bridge

The night's rain had pushed the drain lake at Linden Rise over its path and jammed the reeds against the culvert grate under the ring road. Amara Nwosu stood there with her half-built meter, a box for measuring the signal, the pressure blight put behind her teeth. The reeds had gone black at the root, and the needle jumped whenever she turned toward the grate. Isabel, whom she had asked for help, had not answered.

Across town, Isabel woke in Natalie's flat to an empty bed and the coat gone from the hook. Natalie had slipped out first, so that no one would ask where she was going. Isabel caught her on the bank by the old canal bridge. Natalie halted at her voice, because she had been seen.

Isabel made herself look at Natalie's face and asked whether last night still stood, in daylight.

"It stands," Natalie said.

Then why the bridge, Iz thought. Next time she would be up first.

Amara wrote again, asking to be shown how to cut a nerved blight down to its root. She left out the two cuts she had already made alone, so that Isabel would not refuse her. Isabel agreed to show her when they could meet. Amara turned the phone face down on the wet stone.

Log

  • The night's rain pushed the drain lake at Linden Rise over its path and jammed the reeds against the culvert grate under the ring road, while Amara's half-built signal meter kept jumping and Isabel still hadn't answered. (clean, risky, rolled 6 (one die))
    • Amara Nwosu buoyed
  • Amara sent Isabel a second message asking to be shown how to cut nerved blight, without mentioning the two cuts she has already made alone; Isabel agreed to show her when they can meet. (success-with-cost, risky, rolled 4 (one die))
    • Amara Nwosu ashamed
    • Isabel now believes: That Amara has never cut a nerved blight and is asking how for the first time.
  • Isabel made herself look at Natalie's face and ask whether last night still stands in daylight; Natalie said yes, it still stands, and Isabel could not read anything past the answer. (success-with-cost, risky, rolled 5 (one die))
    • Isabel shaken
  • Natalie slipped out of the flat before Isabel woke and got as far as the canal bridge, where Isabel, who had come looking for her, caught her on the bank above the black water. (failure, risky, rolled 1 (one die))
    • Natalie ashamed
    • Isabel now believes: That Natalie was slipping out to leave her, not going down to the water.
